title: Clause pressure-testing notes
content:
Purpose: quick, scenario-driven scratchpad for "pressure-testing" high-risk contract clauses before escalation. Use during 15–30m pre-call huddles. Not final language — talking points and tolerated fallbacks only.

Topline risk buckets (ranked for this customer):
1) Data residency & export control (HIGH) — customer requires EU-only processing for certain datasets; verify private deployment/KMS options.
2) Model-output IP / derivative ownership (HIGH) — customer asks for assignment vs. license. Avoid assignment; pivot to limited license + auditability.
3) Subprocessors + flow-downs (MED-HIGH) — need transparent subprocessors list + 30d notice for changes for Private/Dedicated.
4) Incident/forensics access & law enforcement (MED) — explicit narrow scope for access, push for warrant+notice provisions when possible.
5) SLA credits & remediation (MED) — settle on service credits up to X% per month; avoid onerous termination for single outage.
6) Security/pen testing & escrows (LOW-MED) — negotiate scope/coordination for pentests + controlled escrow triggers.

Quick scripts (concise):
- Data residency ask: "We can commit to regionally isolated processing via Private/Dedicated deployments with KMS key separation. For hosted, propose contract language that defines categories of data that must remain in EU and a monthly attestation plus audit right."
- IP assignment pushback: "We never assign model weights or derivative IP; propose exclusive license limited to the customer's output data and a standard 'use' right for the deliverables. If they require assignment, escalate to legal with commercial offset (higher fee / escrow / indemnity)."
- Subprocessor notice: "We can provide a current list and 30-day notice of changes. For material subprocessors (hosting, KMS), we will notify and offer mitigation windows; we can discuss a DPA addendum for extra protections."

Pressure-test scenarios (what we ask ourselves before call):
- Scenario A: Customer demands worldwide assignment of all generated outputs + code. Impact: catastrophic for product; mitigation: offer field-limited license, carve out model weights and internal tooling, propose alternative: data export & retention terms that meet their business need.
- Scenario B: Customer insists on quarterly onsite forensics and full access to logs including obfuscated debug data. Impact: privacy + IP leak risk. Mitigation: agree to sanitized logs + scoped session with redacted internals, SOW for onsite support, or remote session under NDA and limited scope.
- Scenario C: Customer wants automatic failover to their cloud + unlimited data pull in event of degradation. Impact: operational complexity, legal exposure. Mitigation: define objective thresholds for failover, limited export formats, and transfer fees; require 14d notice.

Redlines to propose (starter language snippets):
- Data residency: "Provider will process Customer Data in the geographic region(s) specified in Exhibit A. Provider will not transfer Customer Data outside the specified regions except as required by law or with Customer's prior written consent."
- KMS / key control: "For Private deployments, Customer-managed keys (KMS) will be used. Provider will not access plaintext keys and will log key usage; logs may be provided on request for audit purposes subject to mutual NDA and redaction of provider-internal metadata."
- IP: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Input and customer-authored output. Provider retains all rights in the Service, model weights, training code, and derivative infrastructure. Provider grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive license to use the output for its business purposes."
- Subprocessors: "Provider will maintain a current list of subprocessors and will provide at least thirty (30) days' notice prior to engaging any new subprocessor that will process Customer Data. For material changes, Provider will provide mitigation options."

Escalation ladder (who to pull in):
- immediate: Eng on-call (for technical feasibility) + Solutions AE (commercial positioning)
- if persistent: Sr. Legal (Maya) + Head of Product (Samir) + Sales Dir (EM)
- redline blocker: escalate to CFO / CRO for commercial tradeoffs (credits, fees, escrow)

Checklist before offering concessions (mini checklist for call):
- Is the ask implementable in Private/Dedicated vs Hosted? (fast yes/no)
- Does request create product lead/derivative leak risk? (score 1–5)
- Measurable commercial offset identified? (yes/no)
- Escrow/compensating control (KMS, audit, E2E encryption) available? (yes/no)
- Can we offer a time-bound pilot / SOW instead of permanent term? (yes/no)

Notes-to-self / reminders:
- Avoid the word "assignment" without commercial offset. Use "license" language and be ready with sample monetary swaps.
- For customers in regulated finance/health, push Private deployment + independent SOC2/ISO evidence and a narrow DPA exhibit.
- Don't promise feature-level product changes in contract — offer SOW or roadmap commitment instead.
- Keep fallback positions concise: Tiered commitments (hosted -> dedicated -> private) with commensurate fees.

Open questions to resolve pre-call:
- Can infra ops commit to a 30-day notification for subprocessor changes across both hosted and Dedicated? (ask infra)
- What minimal audit log export can we provide without exposing internal debug keys? (ask SRE/observability)
- Template language for key escrow triggers and access (legal to draft sample)

TODOS: (quick)
- Draft 2-line alternative language for IP assignment to use during call (Jordan) — due 2025-01-15
- Confirm KMS logging export feasibility and expected format (Samir) — due 2025-01-17
- Pull current subprocessors list and mark 'material' ones (Maya) — due 2025-01-16

Quick flag matrix (what to do if they push):
- If they insist on assignment -> state firm no; offer higher fee + escrow + limited-scope license instead.
- If they demand worldwide data transfer -> offer targeted export with opt-in plus addendum for law enforcement exceptions.
- If they demand pen-test frequency > annual -> propose SOW for additional tests with third-party operator present.

Shelf language (for later use):
- "Provider will provide an annual attestation of processing location and a one-time export of processing logs in a mutually agreed format."
- "Provider will support reasonable cooperation with lawful requests, subject to Provider's privacy policy and notification obligations unless prohibited by law."

End of scratchpad — use as live notes during negotiation prep. Keep versioning (append date) for each call so we can track patterns of asks across customers.
summary: Personal scratchpad: scenario-based pressure-testing of high-risk contract clauses; scripts, proposed redlines, escalation ladder, and open todos.
